Kim — thanks for the matrix. Quick answers:
- Confirmed: the blue forecast columns match our internal runbook for Q1–Q2. We can firm those numbers.
- Preference: we lean toward a 12-month commit with a 6-month review trigger; we don't want a fully floating index but are open to a capped indexation floor that protects both sides.

We'd like a discount ladder tied to committed tokens: 10% at >= 2B tokens/mo, 18% at >= 4B tokens/mo, and a discretionary 25% at sustained 6+ months of 5B+ (this last one would need exec approval).

I attached our usage export: novagen_usage_q1-q3.csv — should help you validate tiers.

Date: 2026-10-06T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Reserve capacity decision log & escalation pathway — pricing sensitivity notes

Team — I ran sensitivity on NovaGen's numbers. Summary (high level):
- If GPU spot costs spike +30% vs our baseline, realized margin on a fixed discount of 18% drops below our target for >9 months of sustained usage.
- An indexation floor that moves +/- 8% from baseline (quarterly) materially reduces downside.

Proposed commercial constructs to mitigate exposure:
1) Two-tier discount + safety collar: base discount (10%/18%) fixed; above-the-threshold discount (discretionary 25%) paid as a rebate at quarter close and subject to a price-hedge adjustment if GPU index > +15%.
2) Cap on aggregate discount liability: cumulative rebate across the 12-month term cannot exceed X% of committed revenue (model in attached).
3) Approval path: up to 18% — finance and Head of Sales sign-off; >18% up to 25% — requires VP Sales + CFO (Marcus Lin sign-off). Anything over 25% — exec exception tabled to CEO.

I've attached a worked example in procurement_term_sheet_v2.pdf and updated the matrix with breakpoints. Please review and flag where you'd like the collar tightened.

-Aditya

Attachment: procurement_term_sheet_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-08T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Reserve capacity decision log & escalation pathway — option recommendations

Team / Sara — pulling this together into a short decision log so procurement has a clear pick-and-run recommendation. Below are the options I captured from the model:

Option A: 12-month, smaller commit (2B/mo)
- Discount: 10% fixed
- Collar: quarterly indexation +/-8%
- Liability cap: 6% of term revenue
- Approval: straightforward (Sales + Finance)
- Upside: low capital exposure, easy to cancel at renewal

Option B (recommended): 12-month, mid commit (4B/mo)
- Discount: 18% fixed; discretionary 25% rebate for sustained 5B+/mo (paid quarterly)
- Collar: price-hedge triggers only if GPU index > +15% for two consecutive quarters
- Liability cap: 10% of term revenue
- Approval: requires Marcus (CFO) sign-off for discretionary band

Option C: 24-month, large commit (6B/mo)
- Discount: 20% fixed; 25% with exec exception
- Collar: tighter indexation +/-5%
- Liability cap: 12% of term revenue
- Approval: exec review (Marcus + CEO)

Recommended next steps:
1) Sara to confirm final forecast (blue columns) by 2026-10-11.
2) If confirmed, we move Option B to legal for redline with Priya.
3) Marcus to confirm approval for up-to-25% discretionary rebate by EOD 2026-10-11 so sales can present clean term.

Sara — from your note earlier you prefer a capped-index vs. fully floating — Option B preserves that while giving NovaGen a path to the larger rebate.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-11T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Reserve capacity decision log & escalation pathway — approval

Kim / team — I reviewed the options and the downside scenarios in Aditya's PDF. I approve moving forward with Option B under these conditions:
- Discretionary 25% rebate is approved as a quarterly-paid rebate subject to the liability cap (10%).
- Include a price-hedge mechanism that reduces the discretionary band pro rata if the GPU index exceeds +20% for any rolling two-quarter window.
- Legal (Priya) to add a termination-for-material-cost-shock clause that allows both parties to reprice if the index is > +30% across two consecutive quarters.

Priya — please start redlines on the procurement_term_sheet_v2.pdf and the DocuSign-ready term summary. Once we have legal redlines, Kim — you can socialize Option B with NovaGen and request their signature on the redlined term sheet.

Marcus
